findings.text: blocking: merging this change leaves the tree red. The new resume branch supersedes the dispatch behaviour asserted by existing tests: at the reviewed head 939f3a23e my arm over tests/test_reflex_dispatches_one_repair.py, tests/test_repair_skips_out_of_repo_findings.py and tests/test_a_repair_hold_names_its_cause.py gives 13 failed/17 passed/EXIT=1, against 27 passed/EXIT=0 at the pre-change tree, so 13 node ids are added and main goes red on promotion; the node's fence excluded the files it must update, so a scope extension was required before landing.

follow-on: the manifest's follow_ons name ten failing tests across two files, but the change's own population fails thirteen across three — the three in tests/test_a_repair_hold_names_its_cause.py (test_a_repair_held_by_an_exclusion_names_the_exclusion, test_a_repair_whose_only_lane_is_in_harness_is_held_with_a_reason, test_a_spawnable_lane_still_dispatches_the_composition) are named nowhere, so the disclosed impact under-reports by three.

follow-on: a resume the reflex launched is recognised only by its recorded round status, so a resumed turn that ends without answering the findings leaves status "resumed" for the same round_id and the reflex never re-attempts it, whereas the dispatch path re-attempts a died repair through _repair_in_flight (recovery.py:1942); the composed findings ride the one advice and can be lost.
